title: Bank Statement Analysis for Underwriting
summary: Analyse bank statements from PDFs, scans and Account Aggregator data to surface income, obligations, bounces and red flags, with every figure traceable to transactions.

seo.title: Bank Statement Analysis for Loan Underwriting | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that analyses bank statements and Account Aggregator data for income, EMIs, bounces, cash patterns and tampering, with transaction-level evidence.

problem.intro: For self-employed and thin-file borrowers, the bank statement is often the most honest picture of cash flow. Underwriters read months of transactions to estimate income, spot other EMIs, count cheque and NACH bounces and judge whether balances are genuine, while fraudsters edit PDFs or route funds in circles to inflate turnover.

pain_points.title: Formats that vary by bank
pain_points.detail: Statements from different banks, password-protected PDFs, scans and Account Aggregator data each need separate handling before analysis can begin.

pain_points.title: Income hard to separate from noise
pain_points.detail: Salary, business receipts, transfers between own accounts, loan disbursals and cash deposits look similar in narration text.

pain_points.title: Hidden obligations
pain_points.detail: EMIs to other lenders, informal loans and recurring payments are spread across narrations that differ by bank and channel.

pain_points.title: Edited statements and circular flows
pain_points.detail: Altered PDFs, recalculated balances and round-tripping between related accounts are hard to catch by eye.

solution.overview: We build a statement analysis service that accepts e-statement PDFs, scanned copies and Account Aggregator data. It parses transactions, recomputes running balances and checks PDF integrity, then categorises each transaction using rules and a language model that reads narrations in context, including UPI, NEFT, NACH and cheque patterns. The service computes the metrics your credit policy uses, such as average balances on set dates, monthly credits net of own-account transfers, existing EMIs and bounce counts, and highlights red flags like sudden credit spikes, circular transfers or cash-heavy months. Every figure links to its underlying transactions, so the underwriter can verify it before using it in the credit memo.
capabilities: Parses statements from major Indian banks, scanned copies and Account Aggregator FI data
Running-balance recomputation and PDF metadata checks to flag possible tampering
Transaction categorisation for salary, business receipts, transfers, EMIs, bounces and cash
Credit-policy metrics such as average bank balance, net monthly credits and existing obligations
Red-flag detection for circular transfers, related-party flows, credit spikes and window dressing
Underwriter view with every metric drilled down to its transactions

workflow.title: Receive statements
workflow.detail: Statements arrive as uploaded PDFs, scans or consented Account Aggregator data linked to the application.

workflow.title: Parse and verify
workflow.detail: Transactions are parsed, balances recomputed and document integrity checked, with failures flagged.

workflow.title: Categorise transactions
workflow.detail: Rules and a language model categorise each transaction and identify counterparties and recurring patterns.

workflow.title: Compute policy metrics
workflow.detail: Metrics defined in your credit policy are computed per account and across accounts, net of own-account transfers.

workflow.title: Flag risks
workflow.detail: Tamper signals, bounces, undeclared EMIs and unusual flows are listed with linked transactions.

workflow.title: Underwriter review
workflow.detail: The underwriter reviews metrics and flags, corrects categories where needed and uses the output in the credit memo.

inputs: Account Aggregator FI data shared with consent
Applicant's declared income and existing obligations
outputs: Underwriter corrections captured for model improvement
human_in_the_loop: Underwriters review every metric and flag before it enters the credit memo, and the fraud control unit reviews integrity failures. The service never sets eligibility or limits; it provides verified evidence.
integrations: Account Aggregator ecosystem through the lender's FIU integration
Credit bureau data for obligation cross-checks
Fraud or risk case management system
guardrails: Metrics computed by deterministic code; the language model only categorises narrations
Integrity failures always routed to fraud control, never auto-rejected
Account Aggregator data used only for the consented purpose and duration
Statement data masked in logs and retained per policy
compliance_notes: Account Aggregator data is processed within the consent artefact's purpose and retention terms under RBI's NBFC-AA framework.
Supports data minimisation under the DPDP Act 2023 and need-based data collection under RBI digital lending rules.

pilot.scope: Statements from historical self-employed loan files across five or six common banks, compared with underwriter workings, plus a set of known tampered statements.
deliverables: Metric definitions encoded from your credit policy
Working analysis service on historical statements
Tamper detection results on known cases

what_we_measure.how: Parsed transactions and closing balances reconciled with statement totals for each file.
Computed metrics compared with underwriter workings for the same files, with differences explained.
Categories checked by underwriters on a sample of transactions per file.
Known altered statements flagged or missed, and genuine statements falsely flagged.

faqs.q: Do you support Account Aggregator data?
faqs.a: Yes. AA data arrives as structured FI data, so parsing errors disappear and the same categorisation and metrics apply. PDFs remain supported for borrowers who do not use AA.
It checks PDF metadata, fonts, layout consistency and running balances, and flags statements that fail. These are signals for fraud control rather than proof, so every flag is reviewed by a person.

faqs.q: Can we use our own credit policy definitions?
faqs.a: Yes. Metrics such as average balance dates, income netting rules and bounce definitions are configured from your policy and versioned when it changes.
No. It removes manual parsing and counting so underwriters spend their time on judgement. Every figure is traceable, and they can correct categories when context calls for it.
